title: CompactPatch Composer: parameterized runbook artifact generator for safe first-line fixes
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a compiler that converts canonical runbook templates into small, typed, parameterized artifacts called CompactPatches. These artifacts can be executed by first-line engineers via a permissioned CLI or the Console with a dry-run and rehearsal mode. Goals: reduce MTTR for common incidents, ensure auditability and RBAC, enable telemetry-driven suggestions and automatic post-run verification. The feature should support: typed inputs, idempotency checks, precondition gating, optional canary runs, and automated rollback helpers.
acceptance_criteria: A1: CompactPatch compiler accepts a YAML/JSON runbook template and outputs a hermetic artifact with a stable artifact-id and version metadata.
A2: CLI can list/preview CompactPatches, validate parameters locally, and run in --dry-run mode producing a reproducible execution plan.
A3: Execution path enforces RBAC: only roles with 'compactpatch:execute' may run non-dry runs; dry-run available to a wider group.
A4: Every run emits structured audit logs to the ops-audit stream with correlation id that surfaces in Console traces.
A5: Telemetry pipeline captures pre/post metrics and flags regressions to Alerts dashboard; rollout blocked if regression > 5% on safety checks.
A6: Safety harness supports automatic rollback helpers or a one-click revert link in the Console for approved CompactPatches.
A7: Unit + integration tests covering compiler templates, idempotency checks, and RBAC enforced in CI with at least 90% coverage for core logic.
A8: Documentation and runbook gallery published in Confluence and Console help center before GA.
design_notes: Use a small, opinionated schema (namespace, inputs/{name:type:validators}, steps[], preconditions[]) to keep compiler deterministic.
Embed lightweight runtime checks (idempotency tokens, expected-state hashes) to prevent unsafe re-runs.
Prefer declarative step types (query, mutate, wait, call) over arbitrary shell execution; allow exec step only if explicitly privileged.
Execution model: compile -> artifact (static + metadata) -> signed bundle stored in artifact registry -> runtime resolves inputs and runs under a scoped ephemeral role.
Telemetry: include structured 'observability_hint' fields per step to annotate dashboards and SLO checks.

Trade-offs: Restricting step types reduces expressivity but greatly improves safety and testability. We'll prioritize common ops tasks first (restart service, scale, apply k8s patch, run DB migration check) and expand later.
Compatibility: artifacts should be runnable on Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments; runtime uses platform credentials where available and falls back to an approval flow for Closed networks.
Security: artifact signing + KMS integration required. Plan for a security gating job in CI and requirement for security_review_required flag before GA.
implementation_plan: Phase 0 (Discovery, 2w): inventory top 25 runbooks from support logs; define core schema and sample templates.
Phase 1 (Compiler prototype, 3w): implement schema parser, compiler that emits signed JSON bundle, store to artifact-registry service (internal).
Phase 2 (Runtime client + CLI, 4w): implement 'compactpatch' CLI with preview, validate, dry-run, execute; integrate RBAC checks using authn service.
Phase 3 (Console UX + telemetry, 3w): add gallery, preview pane, one-click dry-run, and links to audit traces; wire telemetry to Alerts dashboard and SLO checks.
Phase 4 (Pilot, 3w): onboard two internal teams (oncall, infra) with guarded rollout, collect feedback, iterate templates.
Phase 5 (GA): harden tests, complete docs, security review, and open to wider org.
Backwards compatibility: provide a 'legacy-runbook adapter' shim to convert a small subset of existing ad-hoc runbooks to the new schema as migration assistance.
progress_updates: 2026-01-20: Kickoff meeting w/ PM Priya Mehta and SRE leads (notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/OPS/CompactPatch+Kickoff). Outcome: agree to target top-25 runbooks for Phase 0.

2026-02-05: Prototype compiler v0 commits pushed (GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-tooling/pull/7890). Basic YAML->artifact emit implemented (no signing yet).

2026-02-17: CLI alpha demo to oncall team; they exercised dry-run for 'restart-worker-pool' template. Found UX gap: parameter validation errors were noisy. Filed follow-up ENG-502338 to add typed validators.
2026-02-22: Implemented audit-log emission (pushed GH PR #7943). Added structured correlation id flow between CLI and Console traces. Updated acceptance criteria A4.
reviews: Priya Mehta (PM) - asked for clearer rollback story and explicit canary support; recommended pilot with infra team first.
Evelyn Chen (SRE) - reviewed compiler output; requested idempotency token scheme and step-level 'safety-check' annotations.
Marco Ruiz (Security) - initial review: asked for KMS signing, CI gating, and an allowlist for exec steps. Marked security_review_required = true.
UX (Design) - suggested small Console preview card that shows step-level observability hints and a 'rehearse' toggle for non-privileged users.
notes: Next steps: complete KMS signing integration, add typed validators to schema, and schedule pilot kickoff with infra on 2026-03-02. Consider adding a safepatch 'simulation' runner that replays steps against a snapshot for additional confidence.
